items.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: My family had those recordings on ‘78s, with Martin Green and the D’Oyly Carte, you know this was the 1940s.

ctx.x: Can you recall when you look back on your musical career, your first inspiration to write a song?

No, I can’t. But I can tell you what impressed me as a child musically. I think the first thing that really made me just excited was Gilbert & Sullivan. I just thought that, especially “The Mikado.” My family had those recordings on ‘78s, with Martin Green and the D’Oyly Carte, you know this was the 1940s. And I really listened hard to Gilbert & Sullivan and as a kid, I mean before I was ten or twelve years old, I could sing practically the whole “Mikado” plus other Gilbert & Sullivan stuff too. And I still find…
Oh yeah. And you were in Minnesota?
